history.summary: Ancient Shiva shrine about 2.5 km from the main market in Pauri, on Mount Keenash (Kedarkhand of the Skanda Purana). Believed established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century; the 8th-century date is a traditional attribution, not independently verified. Local lore says Yama performed penance here, giving the older names Kankaleshwar/Kinkaleshwar (from 'kanka', skeleton). The hill-style temple holds a Shiva lingam, Nandi, an ancient drum and idols of Parvati, Ganapati, Kartikeya, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana, with views of the Alaknanda valley and snow ranges. CSV town Pauri is correct; CSV 'state' column holds town names - corrected to Uttarakhand.

name: Kyunkaleshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Pauri is the headquarters town of Pauri Garhwal district, perched on a ridge in the Garhwal Himalaya amid pine and deodar forests, overlooking the Alaknanda valley and snow-capped ranges.

travel.road: About 2.5 km from Pauri main market, near Ransi stadium; walkable from town.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6 AM to 7 PM daily (verify before visiting).
